items.summary: My last post leaned hard on the DB-Engines ranking, and I admitted that ranking measures popularity, not installed base or revenue. Several of you called me on that, politely and otherwise. Fair enough. So this time I went looking for evidence that does not come from one ranking site. Usage surveys: where the money is going, what cloud vendors are building, and what AI tools reach for when nobody tells them what to use. My conclusion has not changed, but I think the case is much stronger than I made it out to be. Beyond DB-Engines The best usage number I can find comes from developers themselves. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey,…

items.summary: Greenlight Financial resolves more than 90% of up to 4,000 monthly security and risk cases without human intervention using Luna, a tiered multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post covers the architecture, episodic memory for continuous learning, and the expansion from SOC operations into financial risk triage.
items.title: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

items.summary: Taxbit built Taxbit Assist, a cited, permission-aware AI assistant embedded in its enterprise dashboard, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post shows how they grounded answers in a curated knowledge base, enforced role-aware and region-compliant safety, and continuously measured answer quality on live production traffic.
items.title: Taxbit Assist: A grounded, role-aware AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

items.summary: PostgreSQL and NUMA, Part 4 of 4 This series covers the specifics of running PostgreSQL on large systems with many processors. My experience is that people spend months often learning the basics when confronted with the problem. This series tries to dispel these difficulties by providing a clear background into the topics in question. The hope is that future generations of database engineers and administrators don’t have to spend months figuring things out through trial and error. This article builds on the content of the previous articles in the series . It assumes both a general working knowledge of NUMA and how NUMA affects PostgreSQL in…
items.title: Chris Travers: PostgreSQL, NUMA, and the Cloud

items.summary: As we built Amazon Quick, its agents grew from answering questions to taking actions, and the same primitives kept getting rebuilt under different names. This post shares the taxonomy we converged on — triggers, agents, capabilities, and learned context — found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When, What, Who, and How.
items.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick

items.summary: An AI agent that acts for a user raises an identity question that per-app OAuth and service accounts leave open: which agent may act for which user, and how you stop it. In this first post of two, you build a task agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that governs access through Okta Cross App Access and AgentCore Identity, and enforces each user's authority.
items.title: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 1
